title: This is what the Perfect Physique looks like (Physical 100 Season 2)
summary: NH reviews Netflix's Physical 100 Season 2, walking through each quest and what it tests. He argues the 'perfect physique' is a well-rounded lean athlete balancing strength, speed, endurance and intelligence, praises the show's supportive fitness culture, and notes the tests' biases.
claims: The perfect physique in a performance sense is the body that dominates in every situation, not the best six-pack or biggest biceps
Season 1's flaw was too little emphasis on stamina; Season 2 fixed it with a cardio elimination on manual treadmills
Manual treadmills are significantly harder than electric ones because you create and maintain your own momentum
The top cardio performers were all lightweights from CrossFit, rugby, soccer and MMA; no strongmen or bodybuilders
Ball-possession fights test will and strength but strip out technical and athletic skill, as most contestants just curl on the ball
Grapplers dominate ground situations; jiu-jitsu technique let even smaller females beat males
In the maze quest, heavy barrels were a trap: heavier but bulkier, so worse economy of space; every team that chased them lost
Picking up and carrying a bag is an underrated fitness skill needing explosive strength plus strong hips and back
Organizing energy matters: a physically dominant team can lose to a lesser crew that paces itself
Strength-heavy tests skew against women, but more finesse-based balance tests would not necessarily favor them either, as the monkey bars showed
Lax pull-up judging (no full lockout or dead hang) favors CrossFitters with kipping; some managed 40 in a minute
In the mine cart quest, the heaviest athletes didn't do best; intermittent-sport light heavyweights with strength-endurance mix excelled, and sled-push experience showed
The show's culture of encouragement between rivals is inspiring; he wants a western version since media shapes society
Some athletes are blatantly on steroids, but the ratio is low and they don't promote drugs, so he is fine with it
The final four all shared a similar lean build with balanced strength, speed, agility, intelligence and endurance
The 'infinite squats' (100 kg x30, 115 kg x40, 200 kg x20...) are pure willpower, the only challenge where a bodybuilder like him could win
Shorter lifters keep an advantage on squats despite height adjustment because of reduced range of motion
In the pole push, keeping your hands low on the pole forces the opponent's center of gravity up; pushing head first backfires
Keeping a cool head under pressure is part of winning in sports
exercises: explosive pick, strong hips and back
fast high reps, but not bodybuilding form
